title: Calendars
tagline: Year 3 — Odd days, leap years, day of the week for any date and repeating calendars

introduction.overview: A calendar problem asks for the day of the week on a given date or the year in which a calendar repeats. The key idea is odd days: the remainder when the number of days is divided by 7. An ordinary year has 1 odd day and a leap year has 2. Century rules give 0 odd days for 400 years, which lets any date be handled by splitting the years.
introduction.placementRelevance: Calendar questions are common short questions in company aptitude papers and need only careful counting.
introduction.realWorldContext: Scheduling, payroll cycles, and software date libraries use the same arithmetic.

learningObjectives: Compute odd days for years, months and centuries
Find the day of the week for a date
Count a given weekday in a month or year

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: There are 7 days in a week. The remainder after dividing days by 7 shifts the weekday.

coreDefinitions: Odd days: remainder when days are divided by 7.
Leap year: divisible by 4; for century years, divisible by 400.
Ordinary year: 365 days (1 odd day). Leap year: 366 days (2 odd days).
100 years have 5 odd days, 200 years 3, 300 years 1, and 400 years 0 odd days.
Odd days of months: Jan 3, Feb 0 (ordinary) or 1 (leap), Mar 3, Apr 2, May 3, Jun 2, Jul 3, Aug 3, Sep 2, Oct 3, Nov 2, Dec 3.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: Each ordinary year shifts the weekday of a date by one day, each leap year by two. Count the shifts and take the remainder by 7.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Count complete centuries, then complete years in the century (with their leap years), then the days of the partial year, add the odd days, and reduce modulo 7.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Day mapping
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: 0 Sun, 1 Mon, 2 Tue, 3 Wed, 4 Thu, 5 Fri, 6 Sat
importantRulesAndFormulas.simpleExample: 3 odd days after Sunday is Wednesday

mainNarrative: In a year of 365 days, 365 = 52 weeks + 1 day, so a date falls one weekday later next year. In a leap year it falls two weekdays later.

Century odd days follow from 100 years = 76 ordinary + 24 leap years = 76 + 48 = 124 odd days, and 124 mod 7 = 5. So 100 years have 5 odd days, 200 years have 3, 300 years have 1 and 400 years have 0.

To find the day of 15 August 1947: the years up to 1900 have 1600 + 300 years, which give 0 + 1 = 1 odd day. In 1901–1946 there are 46 years with 11 leap years, so the odd days are 46 + 11 = 57, which leaves 1. From 1 January to 15 August 1947: 31 + 28 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 15 = 227 days, giving 3 odd days. Total 1 + 1 + 3 = 5, which is Friday.

A calendar repeats when the number of odd days between the two years is 0 and the leap pattern matches. Calendars of 2017 and 2023 are the same (both ordinary, 6 years with 1 leap year gives 6 + 1 = 7 odd days).
The maximum number of Sundays in a year is 53; an ordinary year has 53 Sundays only if it starts on a Sunday, and a leap year if it starts on Saturday or Sunday.

deepDiveAspects.title: Quick year shift
deepDiveAspects.content: Moving forward n years in the same century shifts the day by n plus the number of leap years crossed.

deepDiveAspects.title: Century years
deepDiveAspects.content: Only century years divisible by 400 are leap years; 1900 was not and 2000 was.

shortcutMethods.title: Odd days sum

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Break the span into 400-year (0), 100 (5), 4-year groups, add the odd days and take the remainder by 7.

rulesForApplication: Add the odd days of months.

commonMistakes.mistake: Counting the target year as full

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: The answer day is fixed by odd days mod 7.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: Repeating calendars need equal odd days and leap pattern.

intermediate.question: If 1 January 2021 was a Friday, 1 January 2022 was a
intermediate.explanation: 2021 is an ordinary year, so the weekday moves by one day: Saturday.

advanced.question: The day of the week on 1 January 2000 was
advanced.explanation: The 1999 complete years have 0 + 1 + 4 = 5 odd days (1600 years, 300 years, 99 years with 24 leap years). Adding 1 for 1 January gives 6, which is Saturday.

advanced.question: How many Mondays can a leap year have at most?
advanced.explanation: 366 = 52 weeks + 2 days, so at most 53 Mondays.

placementStyle.question: If the 4th of a month is a Monday, then the 28th of that month is a
placementStyle.explanation: The 28th is 24 days after the 4th, and 24 mod 7 = 3, so Monday + 3 = Thursday.

placementStyle.question: Which year after 2024 has the same calendar as 2024?
placementStyle.explanation: Both must be leap years; the odd days from 2024 to 2052 total 28 years + 7 leaps = 35 ≡ 0.
